topic: At dark as a time of day
claim: Bare NPs for times of day follow at, by, before, until and after, but morning, daytime, evening and dark take in + the instead of at.
evidence_summary: OED quotations with at dark for nightfall: returned at dark with only five men (D. Haig, diary, 1915); We reached Biela at dark (Daily News, 1877); At dark John Henry came to the back door (C. McCullers, The Member of the Wedding, 1946); at daybreak or at dark (Hunting Annual, 1980).
finding: Dark patterns with night and dawn in taking bare at. In the dark is a locative or state expression rather than a time of day. The claim holds for morning, daytime and evening.
proposed_wording: note, however, that morning, daytime and evening take in + the instead of at: in the / ∗at morning
inference: Does dark, as a time of day, take in the rather than at?

evidence.source: Oxford English Dictionary, quotation search for “at dark”.
evidence.example: 1877 We reached Biela at dark (Daily News, under earth-coloured, adj.). 1915 returned at dark (Haig, under dark, n.). 1946 At dark John Henry came to the back door (McCullers, under weekend, n.). 1980 at daybreak or at dark (Hunting Ann., under owling, n.).
evidence.establishes: At dark for nightfall in edited British and American prose across a century.
evidence.locator: Quotation search, 9 results, 4 relevant. Accessed 19 November 2026 through the University of Toronto Libraries subscription.
